text:
sam: heads-up: noticed an uptick in host CPU on streaming hosts after yesterday's microbatch heuristic tweak. p95 CPU up ~14% on ingest boxes.
lee: saw alerts. mostly during long-running streaming sessions where responses are chunked.
nora: was kernel selector touched too?
sam: no, only microbatch heuristic rolled at 02:40 UTC. spike started ~02:47 and stayed on ~20% of nodes.
tim: grabbed a flamegraph from one bad host:
perf snapshot:
assemble_and_normalize   31.0%
kvcache_lookup           14.8%
tokenize_stream          13.6%
http2_frame_read         9.7%
writev_coalesce          4.4%
other                   26.5%

lee: tokenize_stream being that high suggests parse work grew. earlier theory about kernel mismatch causing minibatch stickiness doesn't look primary here.
nora: microbatch changes group by logical boundaries now instead of fixed-timers; might be creating many smaller fragments for typical chat workloads -> lower prefix reuse.
sam: traces show more small-read syscalls on affected hosts (lots of 256-512 byte reads). grpc/hpack decode cost increased.
tim: KV stats show hit-rate slip from ~99% to ~90% in the window for these hosts. that explains extra parsing.
lee: quick repro harness:
```
./chatstream-test --model=model-z --clients=10 --avg-msg=180 --chunk-avg=100 --duration=4m
```

nora: applied two quick canaries: 1) revert microbatch heuristic on canary group A 2) bump kvcache grace to 300ms on canary group B.
sam: initial canary numbers: group B (kvcache bump) saw host CPU drop ~7% and hit-rate back to 95%. group A rollback saw CPU down ~10%. both look promising.
lee: sounds like interplay: microbatching changed fragment rhythm -> more unique prefixes -> kvcache misses -> repeated normalize/tokenize + extra small reads -> CPU tail.
tim: mitigation plan: short-term revert microbatch heuristic for streaming pool; medium-term add an ascii fast-path to tokenizer that skips utf8-normalize when input is plain ASCII; and add telemetry for chunk-size histogram and small-read syscall rate.
nora: i'll add a sampler that records seq-len distribution and fragment-size CDF to help retune heuristics.
sam: lee, can you add a tracer flag whenever microbatcher picks 'logical' mode so we can filter traces?
lee: yep. also will open PR for tokenizer-ascii-skip-normalize. cheap perf win.
tim: post-rollback canary metrics: streaming p95 CPU down 11%, kvcache hit returned to 96% on canary. queueing rollback for full streaming pool.
nora: follow-ups: tim keep kvcache metrics 48h, sam update rollout playbook to require paired kvcache+batcher canaries, lee instrument microbatch telemetry + tracer tag, nora add seq-len hist to observability.
sam: thanks team. will coordinate rollback and schedule a short postmortem to capture lessons. :white_check_mark:
